With sharp sword, they cut him in twain, flinging his body into the road. The warning was ignored.

The massacre began. The second band slaughtered the first. Then, fighting over the booty, they divided and slaughtered each other. 1,000 robbers fought. Then 500. Then 250. Down and down they fought, until only two men remained alive.
The two survivors hid the treasure. One stayed to guard it; the other went for food
In perfect symmetry, greed consumed them both. The guard drew his sword to murder his mate. The forager poisoned the rice to claim it all
The moment the forager returned, the guard cut him down. Alone with the vast treasure, the murderer sat down to eat his poisoned prize. He died then and there.
By reason of the treasure, all had come to ruin

Days later, the Bodhisatta returned with the ransom Finding treasure strewn about and his master’s cloven body, his heart sank His warning had been unheeded With gathered sticks and wild flowers, he built pyre and burnt his master.

Following the bloody road, he found the bodies of the five hundred “Dispatchers.” Then two hundred and fifty. Marking how the thousand had perished, he knew two must have survived. He pressed into the jungle to find them.
At the secret spot, he found ne treasure, the slain forager, and the poisoned guard
Realising the entire story at glance, he mused on the tragedy. Truly, misguided effort destroys not just oneself, but all others involved.
